1	// Runs in Storybook's docgen worker thread (`experimental_docgenProvider`). For a story file it resolves
2	// `meta.component` the way Storybook does, finds that component in a caliper-docgen session, and answers with argTypes
3	// converted by React's rules. Anything it can't document goes to the next provider, React's own.
4	
5	import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises'
6	import { resolve } from 'node:path'
7	import type { RdtComponentDoc } from 'caliper-docgen-napi'
8	import {
9	  STORY_FILE_TEST_REGEXP,
10	  createMetaComponentResolver,
11	  extractDeclaredSubcomponents,
12	  getComponentIdFromEntry,
13	  getStoryImportPathFromEntry,
14	} from 'storybook/internal/common'
15	import { type CsfFile, extractComponentDescription, extractDescription, loadCsf } from 'storybook/internal/csf-tools'
16	import { logger } from 'storybook/internal/node-logger'
17	import type { DocgenMiddleware, DocgenPayload, IndexEntry } from 'storybook/internal/types'
18	import { type ExtractArgTypes, loadExtractArgTypes, toArgTypes } from './arg-types.js'
19	import type { CaliperStorybookOptions } from './index.js'
20	import { DocgenSession, type SessionBinding } from './session.js'
21	import { assertValidOptions } from './validate.js'
22	
23	type Subcomponent = NonNullable<DocgenPayload['subcomponents']>[string]
24	
25	interface StoryFile {
26	  csf: CsfFile
27	  storyPath: string
28	  importPath: string
29	}
30	
31	/**
32	 * `csf`'s story file as the resolver reads it, with `meta.component` being `expression`. The file is parsed again with
33	 * the expression appended as a statement, so every node has source text for the resolver to report an expression it
34	 * cannot follow, and every statement stays: the resolver follows the story's imports and local bindings
35	 * (`const parts = { Item }`) as it does for the written meta, whichever form the meta takes (`export default`,
36	 * `export { meta as default }`, a CSF factory's `preview.meta()`).
37	 */
38	function storyFor(csf: CsfFile, storyPath: string, expression: string): CsfFile {
39	  const code = `${csf.editor.toString()}\n;(${expression})\n`
40	  const parsed = loadCsf(code, { fileName: storyPath, makeTitle: () => 'caliper-docgen' }).parse()
41	  const statement = parsed.program.body.at(-1)
42	  if (statement?.type !== 'ExpressionStatement') throw new Error(`no expression to resolve for ${expression}`)
43	  // The parsed file stands in for the written one, with only its component swapped.
44	  return Object.create(parsed, { _metaAnnotations: { value: { component: statement.expression } } })
45	}
46	
47	/** The resolver threw instead of answering: a defect to hand to the next provider, not a fact about one subcomponent. */
48	class ResolverFailureError extends Error {
49	  override name = 'ResolverFailureError'
50	}
51	
52	/** caliper keeps one value per JSDoc tag; Storybook lists every value. */
53	function tagLists(tags: Record<string, string>): Record<string, string[]> | undefined {
54	  const entries = Object.entries(tags)
55	  return entries.length > 0 ? Object.fromEntries(entries.map(([tag, value]) => [tag, [value]])) : undefined
56	}
57	
58	/** Says there is no component `name` in `path`, and which ones the file does have. */
59	function noComponent(session: DocgenSession, name: string, path: string): string {
60	  const names = session.namesIn(path)
61	  const choice = names.length > 0 ? `; its components are ${names.join(', ')}` : ''
62	  return `caliper-docgen found no component ${name} in ${path}${choice}`
63	}
64	
65	export function createDocgenProvider(
66	  options: CaliperStorybookOptions = {},
67	  binding?: SessionBinding,
68	): DocgenMiddleware {
69	  assertValidOptions(options)
70	  const cwd = process.cwd()
71	  const sessionOptions = {
72	    srcDirs: (options.srcDirs ?? ['src']).map((dir) => resolve(cwd, dir)),
73	    exclude: options.exclude,
74	    tsconfigPath: options.tsconfigPath && resolve(cwd, options.tsconfigPath),
75	    skipHtmlProps: options.skipHtmlProps,
76	    htmlAttributes: options.htmlAttributes,
77	    cache: options.cache,
78	    // Richer than Storybook's own docgen by default: caliper-docgen is fast enough to read the dependencies' types.
79	    loadDependencies: options.loadDependencies ?? true,
80	    collapseInheritedProps: options.collapseInheritedProps ?? 'none',
81	    lazy: options.lazy,
82	    warmUp: options.warmUp,
83	    fillAfter: options.fillAfter,
84	    checker: options.checker,
85	    semanticWaitMs: options.semanticWaitMs,
86	    semanticWaitEmptyMs: options.semanticWaitEmptyMs,
87	  }
88	  // The native binding loads on the first story request, not when Storybook starts the worker.
89	  let sessionPromise: Promise<DocgenSession> | undefined
90	  async function getSession(): Promise<DocgenSession> {
91	    sessionPromise ??= (async () =>
92	      new DocgenSession(sessionOptions, binding ?? (await import('caliper-docgen-napi'))))()
93	    const attempt = sessionPromise
94	    try {
95	      return await attempt
96	    } catch (error) {
97	      // A binding that failed to load is tried again by the next request, not remembered as failed.
98	      if (sessionPromise === attempt) sessionPromise = undefined
99	      throw error
100	    }
101	  }
102	  // A session that cannot start is reported once at a level a developer sees, then every story falls back quietly.
103	  let startFailureReported = false
104	
105	  let started = false
106	  let refreshFailureReported = false
107	
108	  /**
109	   * The session, up to date with the files. A failure before the first successful `fresh()` is a failure to start;
110	   * after it, a failure is a refresh of a running session and is worded as one. Each is reported once until a
111	   * `fresh()` succeeds again, and thrown for the fallback either way.
112	   */
113	  async function freshSession(): Promise<DocgenSession> {
114	    try {
115	      const session = await getSession()
116	      await session.fresh()
117	      started = true
118	      startFailureReported = false
119	      refreshFailureReported = false
120	      return session
121	    } catch (error) {
122	      const { message } = error as Error
123	      if (!started && !startFailureReported) {
124	        startFailureReported = true
125	        logger.warn(`[caliper-docgen] could not start: ${message}; Storybook's own docgen answers instead`)
126	      } else if (started && !refreshFailureReported) {
127	        refreshFailureReported = true
128	        logger.warn(`[caliper-docgen] could not refresh: ${message}; Storybook's own docgen answers instead`)
129	      }
130	      throw error
131	    }
132	  }
133	  const metaComponent = createMetaComponentResolver()
134	  const resolveMeta = (csf: CsfFile, storyPath: string) => {
135	    try {
136	      return metaComponent(csf, storyPath)
137	    } catch (error) {
138	      throw new ResolverFailureError((error as Error).message)
139	    }
140	  }
141	  const fallback = options.fallback ?? 'degraded'
142	  let extractArgTypes: Promise<ExtractArgTypes> | undefined
143	  // A component handed on is reported once, not on every story request that names it.
144	  const reported = new Set<string>()
145	
146	  function reportFallback(key: string, reason: string): void {
147	    if (reported.has(key)) return
148	    reported.add(key)
149	    logger.warn(`[caliper-docgen] ${key}: ${reason}; Storybook's own docgen answers instead`)
150	  }
151	
152	  /** The session key and file `target`'s component points at, or an error that says what the session had instead. */
153	  function locate(session: DocgenSession, target: CsfFile, storyPath: string): { key: string; path: string } {
154	    const resolution = resolveMeta(target, storyPath)
155	    if ('component' in resolution) {
156	      const { path, exportName, localName } = resolution.component
157	      if (!path) throw new Error(`no file for the import of ${exportName}`)
158	      const key = session.resolveExport(path, exportName, localName)
159	      if (key) return { key, path }
160	      // Storybook follows `Select.Option` into the module that declares `Option` and answers with that local name, which
161	      // caliper may know as `Select.Option`.
162	      const member = memberComponent(session, target, storyPath)
163	      if (member) return member
164	      throw new Error(noComponent(session, exportName, path))
165	    }
166	    // A member Storybook cannot follow into a module's source (`Select.Option` of a named import from a barrel).
167	    const member = memberComponent(session, target, storyPath)
168	    if (member) return member
169	    throw new Error(`meta.component: ${resolution.reason}`)
170	  }
171	
172	  /** The sub-component a `Namespace.Member` expression names, when `Namespace` is a named or default import. */
173	  function memberComponent(
174	    session: DocgenSession,
175	    csf: CsfFile,
176	    storyPath: string,
177	  ): { key: string; path: string } | undefined {
178	    const node = csf._metaAnnotations.component as
179	      | {
180	          type?: string
181	          computed?: boolean
182	          object?: { type?: string; name?: string }
183	          property?: { type?: string; name?: string }
184	        }
185	      | undefined
186	    if (node?.type !== 'MemberExpression' || node.computed) return undefined
187	    if (node.object?.type !== 'Identifier' || !node.object.name || !node.property?.name) return undefined
188	    const owner = resolveMeta(storyFor(csf, storyPath, node.object.name), storyPath)
189	    if (!('component' in owner) || !owner.component.path) return undefined
190	    const { path, exportName, localName } = owner.component
191	    const key = session.keyOfMember({ exportName, localName }, node.property.name, path)
192	    return key ? { key, path } : undefined
193	  }
194	
195	  /**
196	   * The session key, file and documentation of the component `name` (default: `meta.component`) names, or why there
197	   * is none. The caller has brought the session up to date for this request.
198	   */
199	  async function component(
200	    csf: CsfFile,
201	    storyPath: string,
202	    name?: string,
203	  ): Promise<{ key: string; path: string; doc: RdtComponentDoc }> {
204	    const target = name ? storyFor(csf, storyPath, name) : csf
205	    const session = await getSession()
206	    const { key, path } = locate(session, target, storyPath)
207	    const { doc, degradedBy } = session.documentation(key)
208	    if (fallback === 'degraded' && degradedBy.length > 0) {
209	      const reason = degradedBy.join('; ')
210	      reportFallback(key, reason)
211	      throw new Error(`${key}'s props may be incomplete: ${reason}`)
212	    }
213	    if (!doc) throw new Error(noComponent(session, key, path))
214	    return { key, path, doc }
215	  }
216	
217	  async function argTypes(doc: RdtComponentDoc): Promise<DocgenPayload['argTypes']> {
218	    extractArgTypes ??= loadExtractArgTypes()
219	    return toArgTypes(doc, await extractArgTypes)
220	  }
221	
222	  async function subcomponent(
223	    { csf, storyPath, importPath }: StoryFile,
224	    { name, componentName }: { name: string; componentName: string },
225	  ): Promise<Subcomponent> {
226	    try {
227	      const { path, doc } = await component(csf, storyPath, componentName)
228	      const { description, summary, jsDocTags } = extractComponentDescription(
229	        undefined,
230	        doc.description || undefined,
231	        tagLists(doc.tags),
232	      )
233	      return { name, path, description, summary, jsDocTags, argTypes: await argTypes(doc) }
234	    } catch (error) {
235	      if (error instanceof ResolverFailureError) throw error
236	      return {
237	        name,
238	        path: importPath,
239	        jsDocTags: {},
240	        error: { name: 'No component import found', message: `${componentName}: ${(error as Error).message}` },
241	      }
242	    }
243	  }
244	
245	  async function document(entry: IndexEntry, importPath: string): Promise<DocgenPayload> {
246	    const storyPath = resolve(cwd, importPath)
247	    const code = await readFile(storyPath, 'utf8')
248	    const csf = loadCsf(code, { fileName: storyPath, makeTitle: () => entry.title }).parse()
249	    // One look at the files for the story and its subcomponents: they are all answered from the same moment.
250	    await freshSession()
251	    const { doc } = await component(csf, storyPath)
252	    const { description, summary, jsDocTags } = extractComponentDescription(
253	      extractDescription(csf._metaStatement, csf.editor) || undefined,
254	      doc.description || undefined,
255	      tagLists(doc.tags),
256	    )
257	    const declared = extractDeclaredSubcomponents(csf)
258	    const subcomponents = Object.fromEntries(
259	      await Promise.all(
260	        declared.map(async (declaration) => [
261	          declaration.name,
262	          await subcomponent({ csf, storyPath, importPath }, declaration),
263	        ]),
264	      ),
265	    )
266	    return {
267	      id: getComponentIdFromEntry(entry),
268	      name: csf._meta?.component ?? entry.title.split('/').at(-1)!.replaceAll(/\s+/g, ''),
269	      path: importPath,
270	      description,
271	      summary,
272	      jsDocTags,
273	      argTypes: await argTypes(doc),
274	      ...(declared.length > 0 ? { subcomponents } : {}),
275	    }
276	  }
277	
278	  return (next) => async (input) => {
279	    const importPath = getStoryImportPathFromEntry(input.entry)
280	    if (!importPath || !STORY_FILE_TEST_REGEXP.test(importPath)) return next(input)
281	    try {
282	      return await document(input.entry, importPath)
283	    } catch (error) {
284	      logger.debug(`[caliper-docgen] ${importPath}: ${(error as Error).message}; asking the next docgen provider`)
285	      return next(input)
286	    }
287	  }
288	}

content.content:
* The tsconfigs, `package.json` files and lockfiles above the session's source directories: a watcher adds them, and
 * passes a change to one to `extractFileIncremental` like any other file, which rebuilds the session. Empty for an
 * unknown session.
 */
export declare function resolutionConfigFiles(sessionId: number): Array<string>

/**
 * What a host needs to answer for one component: its documentation as `sessionDocgenInfo` returns it, and its own
 * diagnostics, each with `affects` set to the key. `{ key: { docgenInfo, diagnostics } }`; a key the session has no
 * component under is left out. A lazy session resolves each requested component now (in parallel), so a host learns
 * whether a component's props may be incomplete from the same call that returns them. Errors for an unknown or closed
 * session.
 */
export declare function sessionComponentAnswers(sessionId: number, keys: Array<string>): string

/**
 * One component as TOON, the compact text an agent reads (`render_component_slice_toon` in the core crate): its prop table
 * with each prop's declaring type, why a prop's type is partly a guess, its inherited layers, and the warnings and
 * errors that say its props may be incomplete. For an in-process host that answers one question about one component
 * and has no use for a project's whole output. `null` when the session has no component under `key`; errors for an
 * unknown or closed session. A lazy session resolves the component now.
 */
export declare function sessionComponentToon(sessionId: number, key: string): string | null

/**
 * The session's components with these keys as react-docgen-typescript documents them (`__docgenInfo`, which
 * Storybook converts to argTypes), as a JSON object keyed by component key. A key the session doesn't have is left
 * out; so is every key before the session is initialized. Errors for an unknown or closed session.
 */
export declare function sessionDocgenInfo(sessionId: number, keys: Array<string>): string

/**
 * Resolves `count` components spread evenly over the session's keys, without returning them: a lazy session then
 * holds the dependency declarations and resolver memos that components share, so the first request a host answers
 * does not load them. With the checker on (the default) it asks the checker for each at background priority, after any
 * story someone opened, and does not wait for it: the answers are kept for the stories that follow. Runs off the
 * calling thread and returns how many components it resolved. An eager session, an unknown session and a count of 0
 * resolve nothing.
 */
export declare function sessionWarmUp(sessionId: number, count: number): Promise<number>

./docs/type-checker-integration.md:105:A long-lived session (the Storybook addon, the lazy `WatchSession`) attaches a warm checker instead of running the whole-project pass above (ADR 0022): a napi session does unless `checker: false`. `caliper-docgen-semantic` keeps one checker warm behind a worker thread, answers from a program rooted at only the requested component's file, and returns its props. The program's snapshot is kept between requests and brought up to date with the files the session says changed ("Watch", below). `WatchSession::component` merges them into the structural answer by name (the checker's type wins, a structural prop the checker did not return stays, and `htmlAttributes` applies once after the merge, as in the structural pass) when they arrive within `semanticWaitMs` (default 150 ms), or within `semanticWaitEmptyMs` (default 2,000 ms, never less than `semanticWaitMs`) when the structural answer lists no props at all (a `ComponentProps<typeof Button>` of a package the structural pass does not model, whose props type it could not expand); otherwise it returns the structural answer plus an `Info` diagnostic, and the checker's late answer serves the next request of the same component while no source file has changed. A kept answer carries what the checker said about the request that made it (a warning that it was not told about an edit, why a component kept its structural result), and every request it serves reports that again, a late answer's included; only an unavailable checker's warning is said once per session. There is one request in flight per component key and content hash of its file: a caller that asks while it is in flight (a story asked while its own prefetch runs, or two stories of one component) waits for that answer, so the checker answers it once. import { appendFileSync } from 'node:fs'

export function createDocgenProvider(options) {
  return (next) => async (input) => {
    const start = Date.now()
    const payload = await next(input)

      appendFileSync(options.log, `${JSON.stringify(row)}\n`)
    }
    return payload
  }
}
